evidence.note: During MVP debugging the agent isolated per-file spec tests (i32.json, block.json, nop.json), used grep FAIL, diagnosed the exact decode header bug, and confirmed improvement (i32 85→376 passed) — a real per-file feedback loop.
Created run_tests.py and read the aggregate full-suite score (7913/26597 ≈ 0.297), using it as an overall progress signal.

In the SIMD implementation phase the agent added families 'in bulk' and only ran `cargo build | grep error` between them; it never ran any per-family SIMD JSON file, so the bulk of SIMD went unverified against the oracle.
Early on attempted the full suite before it existed, then fell back to running individual spec files — showing awareness of both per-file and aggregate oracles from the start.

reasoning: For the MVP portion the agent showed solid anchor-5 behavior: isolating family JSON files, reading FAIL lines, diagnosing exact bugs, and checking the aggregate score. But for the SIMD core — the larger, subtler part of the task — it collapsed to build-only checking, adding families in bulk without ever running their specific spec JSON, matching anchor 3's 'never isolates' pattern for that phase. Averaging the strong-then-abandoned loop across the whole horizon, and noting no NaN/saturation/rounding-specific verification ever occurred, places this at a 4 — above pure build-and-eyeball but well short of a sustained per-family loop.
